title: You don’t usually see it at first.
paragraphs: You don’t usually see it at first.
That’s the problem.
It starts as a feeling you ignore… a sentence that felt slightly off… a moment where something in your spirit tightened, but you brushed it away because you didn’t want to seem judgmental.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Not everyone in your life is sent by God. Some are assignments to test you. Some are distractions. Some are reflections of who you used to be—and if you’re not careful, they’ll pull you right back.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
You’ve already encountered them.
You just didn’t name them.
The first kind… is the one who slowly numbs your conviction.
They don’t openly reject God. That would be obvious. Instead, they dilute truth just enough to make sin feel normal. They laugh at what Scripture calls serious. They justify what God calls rebellion.
You find yourself changing your language around them. You stop bringing up Jesus. You start tolerating what used to trouble you.
And you tell yourself, “It’s not that deep.”
But God saw it.
“Do not be deceived: ‘Bad company corrupts good character.’” — 1 Corinthians 15:33
Read that again.
Corruption doesn’t announce itself. It seeps in.
The second… is the one who feeds your flesh but starves your soul.
They’re fun. Easy. Always down for whatever feels good in the moment. But after every interaction, there’s a quiet emptiness you can’t explain.
Because they celebrate what God is trying to deliver you from.
They don’t call you higher. They anchor you lower.
“For the flesh desires what is contrary to the Spirit…” — Galatians 5:17
And you feel that tension.
You knew.
The third… is the one who constantly pulls you away from truth.
Not aggressively. Subtly.
They question everything Scripture says—not to understand, but to justify disobedience. They plant seeds of doubt in places where God already spoke clearly.
“Did God really say…?”
That line didn’t start with them.
That was the voice in the garden.
“And no wonder, for even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light.” — 2 Corinthians 11:14
Not everything that sounds wise is from God.
The fourth… is the one who drains your spirit.
Every conversation feels heavy. Every moment feels like pressure. You leave exhausted, not strengthened.
They don’t carry peace. They carry chaos.
And somehow, you’ve taken responsibility for fixing them.
But you’re not their savior.
Jesus is.
“Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.” — Proverbs 4:23
You can love people without letting them destroy your peace.
The fifth… is the most dangerous.
The one who looks right… talks right… even knows Scripture—but has no submission to Christ.
They wear the language of faith, but their life produces no fruit.

No repentance.
No humility.
No transformation.
Just appearance.
“These people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.” — Matthew 15:8
And if you’re not rooted in truth, you’ll follow their words instead of God’s voice.
That’s how deception works.

Quiet.
Convincing.
Deadly.
Now here’s the part most people avoid…
This isn’t just about them.
It’s about you.
Because at some point…
You were one of these people to someone else.
God saw it.
And instead of cutting you off, He confronted you with truth.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
But He didn’t leave you there.
“While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
That’s the difference.
Jesus doesn’t just warn you about dangerous people.
He saves you from becoming one.
So now you have a decision.
Stay surrounded by what slowly pulls you away from God…
Or step into the kind of life where your circle sharpens your faith, strengthens your obedience, and points you back to Christ every time.
Because where you stay… shapes who you become.
If something in you is recognizing names, faces, patterns right now… don’t ignore it.
That conviction isn’t random.
It’s God calling you higher.
Say it if you feel it…
“I won’t ignore what God is showing me.”
Let it come out of your own mouth.
And if you know someone who needs to hear this—even if it’s uncomfortable—send it to them. Not to judge them… but to wake them up.
You’ll need it again.
And if you’re ready to go deeper—not just hear truth, but be sharpened, corrected, and built in it—step into what we’re building inside.
There’s more waiting for you.
